subtype: Approach: parting ways with a fair settlement [Revision]
passage:
Coordinator's note, Thursday. Farah writing about Zubin and Vishal, the two founders in our programme.
Over three weeks it became clear they disagreed on a basic point: whether to sell customer contact lists to outside firms. Vishal wanted to, and Zubin would not. Neither would move.
I did not push either way. I sat in on their meetings and reminded them to list what each had done and what was left. They agreed Zubin would leave, with a fair share for the eight months of work, and a four-week handover of accounts and passwords. I suggested each ask their own lawyer to read the paper.
On Friday they signed and shook hands. Zubin's eyes were wet but steady, and they went for tea together after.
— Farah

qa.q: How long was the handover of accounts and passwords?
What was Zubin probably feeling when signing the exit paper?
qa.a: Zubin was sad but at peace: the wet but steady eyes and going for tea afterwards show grief without bitterness.

qa.q: What could the founders do if they later disagree about the handover?
qa.a: They could go back to the signed paper and, if it does not cover the point, ask a neutral person to help them talk it through.

qa.q: How might the programme staff who work with both founders have seen the parting?
qa.a: The staff saw a clear, calm exit with a handover plan, so they knew who to work with and could keep their jobs going without taking sides.

grounding: The note shows founders who disagree on a basic value negotiating a clear exit with fair shares and a handover, and staying on speaking terms.

subtype: Approach: parting ways with a fair settlement [Revision]
passage:
Himani's diary, 30 November.
Signed the exit papers with Gautam today. It's over, and somehow we're still friends.
It started in August, when he wanted to take the big contract from the mining company and I couldn't. Our whole company is supposed to be about clean water. We argued for weeks. Neither of us was wrong, exactly; we just want different things from this company.
So instead of a war, we sat with our mentor and a lawyer and worked it out. He keeps the company and the mining deal. I get a fair amount for my shares, based on the two years I put in, paid over a year. I stay till January to hand over the supplier contacts and train the new operations person.
When we left the lawyer's office, Gautam bought us both chai and said, "Call me when you start the next one." I will.

qa.q: Until when will Himani stay to hand over?
How does Himani feel after signing the exit papers?
qa.a: Himani feels sad it's over, but relieved and warm that they are still friends.

qa.q: Which parts of the exit made it fair?
qa.a: Payment for two years' work spread over a year, a clear handover till January, and working it out with a mentor and a lawyer.

qa.q: How might Gautam feel about the way they parted?
qa.a: Gautam seems grateful and friendly, buying chai and asking to hear about the next venture.

grounding: It shows co-founders whose values differ negotiating a clear exit with fair shares for work done and a handover, staying friends instead of going to court.

Reena: I read the lawyer's draft. I think it's fair
Tushar: me too. honestly I thought this would end in a shouting match
Reena: we did shout. in August 😅
Tushar: true. but I get it now. you want the NGO partnerships, I want to go fully commercial. we can't both steer
Reena: yes. so: you keep the company, I get paid for my shares for the 2 yrs over 12 months, and I hand over the NGO contacts by March
Tushar: and you stay listed as co-founder on the website. you built it
Reena: that means a lot tbh 🙏
Tushar: can we still do our Friday dosa?
Reena: only if you pay till the settlement clears
Tushar: deal

qa.q: By when will Reena hand over the NGO contacts?
What does "that means a lot" show about Reena's feelings?
qa.a: Reena feels touched and respected that the work is still credited.

qa.q: What made this exit calmer than a court fight?
qa.a: They named the real difference in values, used a lawyer's draft, and agreed fair payment, a handover date and continued credit.

qa.q: How does Tushar see the split now?
qa.a: Tushar understands they can't both steer and is relieved it didn't end in a shouting match.

grounding: It shows co-founders with a basic difference in values agreeing a fair exit with payment for work done and a handover plan, and staying on good terms.
